title: Tempo Checkpoint Lane and Annotated Release Docket — Aug 2027
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-first release docket focused on tempo checkpoints (smallish, frequent windows) rather than big-batch launches. Aim: reduce blast radius by 24–48h incremental ramps, provide a compact operator checklist, and ship a skeletal release notes draft to hand to docs/GTM after final review.

Scope and context:
- Surface: hosted API feature flag for 'streaming-chunked-metadata' + runtime kernel pick optimization for L2 sequence shapes.
- Customer impact profile: low-medium; potential latency regression in long-stream workloads if kernel fallback triggers.
- Target window: 2027-08-17 00:00 UTC — multi-region, staged by region (NA -> EU -> APAC).

High-level rollout calendar (checkpoint lanes):
- T-minus 72h (2027-08-14): code freeze for non-critical changes; release artifact bake starts. Owner: build/releng.
- T-minus 48h (2027-08-15): integration smoke (end-to-end), perf bench at nominal traffic, draft release notes live. Owner: SRE + Perf Eng.
- T-minus 24h (2027-08-16): stakeholder sync (PM/SE/Docs/GTM); preflight checklist signoffs. Owner: release lead.
- T-minus 2h (2027-08-16 22:00 UTC): final canary triggers in small NA cohort (1% traffic). Watch 30m.
- T+1h: if canary green, escalate to 10% NA. Watch 2h.
- T+6h: 50% NA if steady; automated rollback window for 1h after each step.
- T+12h: full NA, begin EU canary at 5% (staggered by region).
- T+24–48h: APAC ramp and final global stable.

Preflight checklist (quick pass, annotated):
- Artifacts
  - [ ] Build artifact SHA: confirm tag and checksums (deploy team). NOTE: use immutable tag format rel/2027.08.17-aisha.
  - [ ] Container image scanned and vulnerabilities triaged (<S0, S1 only).
- Configuration
  - [ ] Feature flag toggles created in FF service and scoped to canary cohort.
  - [ ] Model routing mapping updated for kernel_variant field (defaults preserved).
- Observability & Telemetry
  - [ ] New trace span added for "streaming-chunked-metadata" path. Verify sample rate set to 1% for canary.
  - [ ] Latency SLO dashboards updated: p50/p95/p99 charts + token-per-second ingestion chart.
  - [ ] Cost-per-token sampling enabled for canary traffic.
- Safety nets
  - [ ] Automated rollback policy exists (canned) tied to latency > 2x baseline or error rate > 0.5% over 5m.
  - [ ] Manual kill switch in ops-console documented and tested in dry-run.
- Compatibility
  - [ ] Backwards compatibility tests run for SDKs (python/js) — basic smoke passes.
- Comms
  - [ ] Slack channel #release-tempo pre-warmed with owners listed.
  - [ ] Customer success + on-call SEs notified for high-value accounts on the canary cohort.

Canary watchlist (metrics to watch immediately):
- request latency (stream-open, first-token, per-token) p50/p95/p99
- error rate (4xx/5xx) overall and by model variant
- token throughput vs. baseline and cost/tok sampling
- memory/GPU utilization on canary pods (OOMs, kernel fallback logs)
- trace error samples and top stack traces
- rollback triggers observed: count and reason codes

Rollback decision ladder (operational cheat-sheet):
- Automatically rollback if latency p95 > 2x baseline for 10m AND error_rate_delta > 0.2% (auto-rule).
- Manual immediate rollback if any of: persistent OOMs on 2+ pods, cascading request failures to dependent services, or a customer-reported production outage.
- Post-rollback: create immediate postmortem stub in Confluence and notify #incidents. Owner: release lead + pod oncall.

Post-launch smoke + 24h watch checklist:
- Verify logs for kernel-fallback churn (expect <0.1% fallbacks).
- Validate model outputs on a 50-case golden prompt set for regressions. Automated run by eval harness.
- Confirm billing sampling shows expected cost delta < 5% on dev cohort.
- Docs: handover release notes to Docs owner (Priya) with callouts (features, opt-in flags, known issues).

Draft release notes (skeleton — copyable to final sheet):
Title: Streaming-chunked-metadata + kernel-pick optimization (Aug 2027)
Summary: This release introduces server-side chunked streaming metadata for multi-part responses and runtime kernel-selection improvements for L2-shaped sequences. Together these reduce token tail latency for common streaming workloads and provide a fallback-safe kernel path for atypical sequence lengths.
What’s new:
- server: chunked metadata streaming: embeds per-chunk metadata (latency hints, chunk id). Enabled behind FF.
- runtime: kernel picker: picks optimized kernel based on observed sequence shape, with conservative fallback to generic kernels for safety.
Bug fixes / improvements:
- reduced locking in KV cache path which reduced p50 token latency by ~6% in microbench.
- tightened telemetry sampling to surface cost anomalies promptly.
Known issues / gotchas:
- In rare long-stream sessions (>10k tokens), the kernel picker may opt fallback kernels more often, increasing p99 by up to 8% in synthetic stress. We have a mitigation plan (rolling config throttle) to tune over the first 48h.
Migration / rollout notes for customers:
- Feature disabled by default for existing cohorts. Customers on Dedicated can request early enable via SE.
- SDK changes: none required; metadata appears in stream envelopes (backwards compatible).

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- QA: expand golden prompt set to include 6 longer conversation threads (Benicio).
- Perf: run 24h continuous perf harness against NA canary config and capture baseline drift (Tom).
- Docs: finalize example streaming envelope snippet and include a short snippet for customers parsing chunk metadata (Priya).
- Post-release: schedule follow-up retro 72h after full global rollout. Owner: release lead.

Field notes / friction log (working):
- 2027-08-05: early bench showed kernel choice improved avg-case by 9% but caused jitter in long-tail synthetic runs — flagged to runtime team.
- 2027-08-09: FF service change required small migration; validated in staging.
- 2027-08-10: added additional trace span and lowered sampling for canary to avoid noise.

Attachments / quick links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234 (rollout decision doc)
- Jira epic: JIRA-RL-6812 and child tickets: RL-6821, RL-6830 (perf), RL-6835 (docs)
- GitHub: runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/402

Final notes (tone & release intent):
- Keep this tempo lane conservative: prefer slower but observable ramps. If in doubt, hold and run more perf sampling rather than accelerate.
- Primary aim: keep customer-facing regressions at zero; improve median token latency for streaming users incrementally.

-- end docket --
